description: CFNAI row dated 2020-04-01 (= reference month March 2020, value = -18.28) is the COVID-month reading released by Chicago Fed ~Apr 23 2020 (BEA convention: month-X CFNAI published ~25 days after month-X end). Code in 96_5way_retrain_v3f_us_macro.R lines 74-83 does nafill(LOCF) + shift(1L), making this value visible on 2020-04-02 → ~21-day lookahead during COVID crash.
recommendation: Apply explicit publication_lag_days shift (e.g., 25 days for CFNAI). Pattern: row dated month-end Date → release on Date + 25d → panel sees value at panel_date >= Date + 25d. ECOS builder (134_ecos_fetch_kr_macro.R lines 234-256) already uses this pattern: series_shifted[, Date := Date + pub_lag_days] + rolling join.

description: ICSA (Initial Claims) FRED rows are dated Saturday week-ending day. Actual release: Thursday 08:30 ET (~22:30 KST) of following week (5-day delay). In 96_5way_retrain_v3f_us_macro.R, nafill(LOCF) + shift(1L) makes Sat row visible Mon-Tue, which is 3-5 days BEFORE actual release. ICSA 4-week MA inherits this leakage.
recommendation: Shift ICSA raw date by +5 calendar days (Sat → following Thursday): icsa[, Date := Date + 5L]. Then rolling-fill + shift(1L).

description: Init_Claims (= ICSA) in fred_macro_wide.parquet is dated Saturday week-end. BBVA builder (A6_bbva_macro_builder.R line 71-75) calls zoo::na.locf + diff + shift(1L). This produces 4-5 day lookahead via same convention bug as ICSA.
recommendation: Apply +5 day shift on Init_Claims before LOCF. Same fix as ICSA. Alternatively: rebuild fred_macro_wide.parquet with release-date convention.

description: FRED fetch (95_fred_us_macro_fetch.py:35) uses the latest fredgraph.csv endpoint with no realtime/vintage/as-of parameters. For revised FRED series (CFNAI, IndProd, M2, CPI, all routinely revised 1-12 months post-initial release), historical rows in fred_us_macro_daily.csv contain post-date REVISIONS, NOT the values that were actually known at past decision dates. Separate current-vintage PIT risk beyond the publication-lag bugs.
recommendation: Switch to ALFRED (Archival FRED) endpoint with vintage_dates parameter: https://alfred.stlouisfed.org/series?seriesid=X&vintage_dates=YYYY-MM-DD. For each panel decision date, use as-of vintage published by that date. Alternatively: fetch + log series snapshot per release date and reconstruct release-time-correct series.
magnitude: Variable. Typically small (<5% revision) but can be ~10-20% for IndProd / M2 / CPI during recession start months. Compounds with publication-lag bug for CFNAI.
